author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Canadian oil producers Tamarack Valley and Headwater Exploration agreed to merge in an all-stock transaction valued at C$10 billion, or about $7.25 billion, the companies said Tuesday.

Reuters reported that Headwater investors would receive one Tamarack share for each share held. Existing Tamarack shareholders would own 66.5% of the combined company, while Headwater shareholders would hold 33.5%.

The deal would combine major positions in Alberta’s Clearwater Formation and is expected to close in the fourth quarter, subject to approvals. Tamarack also plans to raise its quarterly dividend 20% to C$0.06 a share and spin non-core assets into a separate listed company.

Reuters reported that Tamarack shares gained more than 4% and Headwater nearly 2% after the announcement. Those moves reflect trading at the time of the report, not live prices. Investors will now weigh expected scale and pipeline access against integration risk, commodity-price exposure and the possibility that transaction terms or timing change before closing.
dek: The all-stock transaction would create the largest publicly traded producer focused on Alberta’s Clearwater Formation.
headline: Tamarack and Headwater agree to $7.25 billion oil merger
